## Active

### D-660 — Prose is a template rendered on demand, never stored

> _2026-10-28 · realm/blong-feedback · active_

The Markdown a coding agent receives is rendered from the stored rows by one injected library
function in adapter/db, so the same rows always produce the same document and a tap test can assert
it. Nothing about the document is persisted: a session row holds only what the person submitted, the
status and the processing stamp, so a wording corrected later is what the next render shows and no
stored text can go stale. The wording is kept verbatim as a quote under a heading that carries the
logical id and the visible label, and the renderer prefers the reviewer clarification over the
original comment when one exists, because the point of the review is to make the report actionable.
An LLM is not required and is not called by default: the adapter config names an optional polish
method, handed the rendered document and returning a rewritten one, which is applied to the response
and never written back.

### D-663 — Prose is rendered for a batch of unprocessed sessions

> _2026-10-28 · realm/blong-feedback · active_

A reviewer works through a queue, not one row at a time, so the render takes a selection rather than
a session: either an explicit list of ids or the status new, which is the unprocessed queue. Marking
is a separate bulk call that stamps status, the reviewer resource and the time on exactly the named
sessions, so the queue shrinks only when a person says it should and a render itself never mutates
anything. That split is what makes a render safe to repeat, cheap to preview and impossible to lose:
an administrator who renders twice sees the same document, and one who edits a wording sees the
correction in the next render. Empty output is a meaningful answer, because it says the queue is
clear.

### D-665 — The prose method is feedback.prose.render, three segments

> _2026-10-28 · realm/blong-feedback · active_

It began as feedback.session.prose.render, which reads best, and the gateway answered 404 for it: an
external route is /rpc/{subject}/{object}/{predicate} and the client turns every dot of the object
into a path separator, so a four-segment name reaches /rpc/feedback/session/prose/render and matches
no route. The handler is feedbackProseRender in adapter/db and gateway/feedback, the capability
seeds, the suite's portal.feedback.prose, and the review page's default. Anything that gains a
fourth segment later hits the same wall; the rule is that the wire name has three parts.

### D-670 — A capture is stored at CSS size and shown no larger than itself

> _2026-10-29 · realm/blong-feedback · active_

Two complaints led here. A picture left at the surface device pixels is drawn at two or three times
the size the person saw, so capture.ts now folds the frame-to-viewport ratio into its scale and the
stored shot is CSS-sized. And the page drew every shot at the pane width, which magnified a small
crop into a zoom nobody asked for; it now caps the picture at its own natural width, which also
keeps the fraction-positioned boxes on their elements because the container is the image. The two
panes wrap below roughly 900 pixels — PrimeFlex marks flex-1 as important, so the detail pane
carries its basis inline and drops the class — because a reviewer on a laptop was reading a
190-pixel column.

### D-671 — The review story shows a real submission, not a mock screen

> _2026-10-29 · realm/blong-feedback · active_

The fixture drew an inline SVG of a grey table, which is why the review page looked invented beside
a real capture: the boxes landed on rectangles that only claimed to be a header and a field.
img/feedbackShot.jpg is now the JPEG the last real submission stored — the club browse table header
— and every anchor and callout fraction in the fixture is copied from that submission rows, so the
boxes land where they were drawn and the document beside them names the same identifiers. The
picture is a frozen copy rather than a fetch: a story that called a database would not be a story.

### D-672 — The review page edits the callouts in place

> _2026-10-29 · realm/blong-feedback · active_

A reviewer had one panel of the picture and a second list of comment fields beside it, and the user
reading it called the second list clutter: the comment belongs where the person put it. The stored
boxes are now the editor — the bevel drags, the corner resizes, the text area saves on blur, the x
closes — and each act is one feedback.item.edit call carrying refinedText, callout (fractions) or
removed. Closing sets removedAt rather than deleting the row, so the persons words survive and the
prose skips them; closing is undoable from a row of chips under the pane. The drag and resize reuse
moveBox, resizeBox and MIN_CALLOUT from blong-browser, which is why they are exported, and the
connectors are drawn in the picture pixel viewBox with arrowHeadPoints: the old hundred unit box
stretched to the picture aspect turned every arrowhead into an ellipse.

### D-675 — The review story runs on a fake realm that applies its edits

> _2026-10-29 · realm/blong-feedback · active_

The story answered every call from a fixed set of values, including a hard-coded document, so a
reader who rewrote a comment and pressed Generate prose saw the old wording and concluded the
feature was broken — the user did exactly that. The answers are now a small stateful fake in
src/stories/feedbackReviewStub.ts: feedback.item.edit mutates an in-memory list and
feedback.prose.render runs the realms own renderProse over it, so the story behaves like the page
does against a database. The fake lives in its own module because the tap entry imports it (a story
file is not importable from Node) and because the picture it used to import is the one value a
bundler mints and Node refuses: the shot is now passed in, and only feedbackReviewShot.ts touches
the jpg.

### D-697 — blong-feedback runs no Playwright leg of its own

> _2026-10-30 · realm/blong-feedback · active_

The realm's `ci-test` is `blong-dev test` and nothing else. Its `test/` folder holds no Playwright
spec, so the second leg failed with `Error: No tests found` and exit 1 in build 648, and it
published nothing: the tap leg had passed its 16 tests, so the report carried a green slice and no
reason for the operation being red.

The page is covered end to end where it is actually served — blong-sport's `test/feedback.play.ts`
walks the feedback mode, the callouts, the crop, the submission and the review page — so a second
leg here would duplicate it. A spec added here later has to put the leg back in the script.
